**Issue #4196 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4196: Patch: every pull request's perf smoke holds the two budgets that need no clock, a seat's view size and the replay fold's length, instead of judging none
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Every pull request already runs a quick speed check on the game engine. Besides timings, it measures two things that come out exactly the same on every run: how much data the game sends one player for one board, and how many moves the longest of its test games takes to replay. The quick check works out both numbers and then ignores them. Only the next daily run compares them with their limits, and a daily run that fails holds up the next release to players until someone fixes it. Once this is built, a change that doubled what each player is sent, or made the test games run far longer, fails its own pull request, in front of its author, the same day. Today it turns up in the next morning's daily run.

## Why

- `crates/tools/src/perf.rs:592` reads `let failures = if smoke { Vec::new() } else { judge(&measures) };`, so `--smoke` judges no budget at all. Yet the module header (`perf.rs:12-13`) says the two work measures, each `view_for`'s JSON bytes and the fold's `reduce` calls, "need no clock and cannot flake", and both budgets hold "at either profile" (`perf.rs:97-102`).
- The smoke run already computes both exactly as the judged run does. The bytes are taken once per state, outside the timed passes (`perf.rs:570-575`), and the fold's calls are the corpus game's log length (`perf.rs:587`), so neither depends on how many passes run.
- The per-pull-request test, `perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once` (`crates/tools/tests/perf.rs:37-63`), asserts `failures == []` (line 43), which cannot fail today. The judged run, `perf_holds_every_budget` (lines 65-72), is `#[ignore = "daily: …"]`. It runs only in `super.yml`'s daily tests on `_staging`, where a red run blocks production's promotion and comes back to the bot as `priority:high` (`super.yml`'s header). There have been 16 "daily super run failed" fixes since 2026-10-20 (`git log --grep`).
- The per-pull-request test already runs on every change to the engine, cards, AI, dungeon run, shared logic or tools: it is in the `tools, wasm` group (`.github/ci/rust-test.toml:170-173`), which `scripts/ci-scope.sh:331-337` turns on. Judging there needs no workflow change.
- The work measures drift and nobody sees it. On `main` at 8c6074f25b, `target/release/jackioh perf --smoke` gave the same values on all three runs: `view_for bytes` median 7,001 (budget 14,000), and `fold reduce calls` 404 (budget 520, now 78% of it). The budget's comment (`perf.rs:100-102`) records 256 calls (fuzz seed 37), measured on 2026-11-09. The corpus's longest game is now seed 29's, at 404 actions: 58% longer after nine days of card changes, and no pull request saw it move.

## Proposal

1. In `perf.rs`, give `Measure` a way to say whether it needs the clock: the five timings do, `ViewForBytes` and `FoldReduceCalls` do not. Under `--smoke`, judge only the rows that need no clock: `failures` lists a crossed work budget and the command exits 1, as a judged run does. The full run still judges all seven. Smoke stays one pass, so the per-pull-request time does not change.
2. The smoke table's first line says the clock budgets were not judged, in place of `smoke: no budget judged`, so the report says what it held.
3. Tests:
   - A unit test beside `every_measure_over_its_budget_fails_naming_its_median_p95_and_budget` sets every row at twice its budget and checks that the smoke verdict names exactly `VIEW_FOR_BYTES_BUDGET` and `FOLD_REDUCE_CALLS_BUDGET`. Another sets every row at its budget and checks that it passes.
   - `perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once` then holds today's corpus to both work budgets, and checks each of the two rows' medians against its budget by name.
4. Docs:
   - The `perf.rs` module header, the README's `perf` row (`--smoke` "judges nothing" becomes "judges the two work budgets") and `tests/perf.rs`'s header.
   - The daily test's `daily:` reason names the per-pull-request test as what holds the work budgets on every pull request. `acceptance.rs` requires every `daily:` reason to name that.
   - The work budgets' comments record today's reading (7,001 bytes; 404 calls, fuzz seed 29) beside the calibration's. The budget values stay as they are: loosening 520 to twice today's reading is the decision this leaves out.

Out of scope, for a person: no workflow runs `jackioh perf` at release, so the `*_RELEASE` time budgets are judged only when someone runs `cargo jackioh perf` by hand. Holding them in CI would take a workflow line.

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/perf.rs`: `Measure`, `measure()`, `judge`, `perf_table`, its unit tests and the work budgets' comments
- `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs`
- `crates/tools/README.md`: the `perf` row
- No SPEC section or ruling: the budgets are tooling (#3429), and no game rule changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Under `--smoke`, a `view_for bytes` or `fold reduce calls` row over its budget is a failure that names its constant, and the run exits 1 (a unit test over rows).
- [ ] Under `--smoke`, none of the five timings is a failure, even at twice its budget (the same unit test).
- [ ] The full run still fails each of the seven measures over its budget: the existing unit tests are unchanged and pass.
- [ ] `perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once` passes on today's corpus. The pull request reports one manual run in which a work budget set below today's value fails it.
- [ ] The README row, the module header, the test header and the `daily:` reason each say what the smoke run judges.
- [ ] These pass: `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf`, `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh perf::`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`.

## Size and risks

Small: about 40 to 60 lines across one module, its integration test and one README row; `difficulty:medium`. No player-facing change and no engine change.

The intended effect is the only risk. A pull request that means to grow the view, or lengthen the corpus's longest game, past twice the calibrated value now fails its own CI and re-measures the budget, as `perf.rs`'s comment already asks, instead of failing the daily run. The fold-calls measure is the length of the longest random-policy game of seeds 1 to 40, so a card change can cross it without making the engine any slower. Today it sits at 404 of 520, and such a pull request would re-measure it as `perf.rs` describes.

The timings stay daily-only: one pass on a shared runner is too noisy to judge.
```

## Goal

Under `--smoke`, `cargo jackioh perf` judges the two deterministic work measures (`VIEW_FOR_BYTES_BUDGET` and `FOLD_REDUCE_CALLS_BUDGET`) that require no clock and cannot flake, while leaving the five timing measures unjudged, exiting 1 if either work budget is crossed. The smoke table reports `; smoke: clock budgets not judged` in place of `; smoke: no budget judged`, and the work budgets' comments, docs, and test annotations record that smoke runs hold the work budgets on every pull request. Unit and integration tests verify both that crossing either work budget in smoke mode fails with the proper constant name and that timing budget violations remain ignored under smoke.

## Files to touch

| File | Status | What changes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `crates/tools/src/perf.rs` | change | Add `needs_clock()` to `Measure`; add `#[serde(skip)] needs_clock: bool` to `Row`; implement `judge_smoke()`; update `measure()` to call `judge_smoke()` when `smoke` is true; update `perf_table()` header string to `; smoke: clock budgets not judged`; update module doc header, `Args::smoke` doc comment, and budget comments for `VIEW_FOR_BYTES_BUDGET` and `FOLD_REDUCE_CALLS_BUDGET`; update existing table test and add unit tests for smoke judging. |
| `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs` | change | Update file doc header; in `perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once`, assert `"view_for bytes"` and `"fold reduce calls"` medians are at or below their budgets; in `perf_holds_every_budget`, update `#[ignore]` reason to name that `perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once` holds the work budgets on every pull request. |
| `crates/tools/README.md` | change | In the `perf` row of the commands table, change `--smoke` description from "judges nothing" to "judges the two work budgets". |

Must not touch: `crates/engine/`, `crates/cards/`, `crates/ai/`, `crates/run/`, `crates/server/`, `crates/shared/`, `apps/`, `spec/`, `.github/`, `.harness/`, or any other directory.
Spec sections and rulings: Tooling only (#3429, #4196). No game rules change and no new ruling is required.

## Steps

1. **Add `needs_clock` to `Measure`** in `crates/tools/src/perf.rs`:
   Inside `impl Measure`, add method:
   ```rust
   fn needs_clock(self) -> bool {
       match self {
           Measure::Reduce
           | Measure::ViewFor
           | Measure::LegalActions
           | Measure::HashState
           | Measure::Fold => true,
           Measure::ViewForBytes | Measure::FoldReduceCalls => false,
       }
   }
   ```

2. **Add `needs_clock` field to `Row`** in `crates/tools/src/perf.rs`:
   Add `#[serde(skip)] needs_clock: bool` to `struct Row`.
   In `fn row(measure: Measure, mut samples: Vec<f64>) -> Result<Row>`, set `needs_clock: measure.needs_clock()`.
   In `mod tests` helper `fn row_at(measure: Measure, value: f64) -> Row`, set `needs_clock: measure.needs_clock()`.

3. **Implement smoke row judging** in `crates/tools/src/perf.rs`:
   Add `judge_smoke`:
   ```rust
   /// Under `--smoke`, judge only the rows that need no clock.
   fn judge_smoke(rows: &[Row]) -> Vec<String> {
       let unclocked: Vec<Row> = rows.iter().filter(|r| !r.needs_clock).cloned().collect();
       judge(&unclocked)
   }
   ```
   `judge(&[Row])` remains unchanged so full runs still evaluate all 7 measures with identical formatting.

4. **Update `measure()` for smoke judging** in `crates/tools/src/perf.rs`:
   Change line 592 from:
   ```rust
   let failures = if smoke { Vec::new() } else { judge(&measures) };
   ```
   to:
   ```rust
   let failures = if smoke { judge_smoke(&measures) } else { judge(&measures) };
   ```
   When `failures` is non-empty, `run()` already bails with exit code 1 naming the crossed budgets.

5. **Update smoke table header** in `crates/tools/src/perf.rs`:
   In `fn perf_table(report: &Report) -> String`, change:
   ```rust
   if report.smoke {
       out.push_str("; smoke: no budget judged");
   }
   ```
   to:
   ```rust
   if report.smoke {
       out.push_str("; smoke: clock budgets not judged");
   }
   ```
   In `mod tests`, update `the_table_has_a_line_per_measure_under_its_header()`:
   Change `assert!(lines[0].ends_with("; smoke: no budget judged"), "{table}");` to `assert!(lines[0].ends_with("; smoke: clock budgets not judged"), "{table}");`.

6. **Update doc comments and budget comments** in `crates/tools/src/perf.rs`:
   - Module doc header (line 11-12): change `(one under\n//! \`--smoke\`, which judges no budget)` to `(one under\n//! \`--smoke\`, which judges the two work budgets)`.
   - `Args::smoke` doc comment (line 112): change `/// Time the corpus once and judge no budget (the per-pull-request smoke test).` to `/// Time the corpus once and judge the two work budgets (the per-pull-request smoke test).`.
   - Comments on `VIEW_FOR_BYTES_BUDGET` and `FOLD_REDUCE_CALLS_BUDGET` (lines 97-102): record today's readings beside the calibration values:
     - `/// The JSON size of one seat's \`view_for\`, in bytes, at either profile: a median of 6,976 in all six\n/// runs (7,001 on 2026-11-18), 2x headroom.`
     - `/// The \`reduce\` calls the fold of the longest corpus game makes (its log's length), at either\n/// profile: 256 in all six runs (fuzz seed 37; 404, fuzz seed 29, on 2026-11-18), 2x headroom.`
     Keep the budget constants at `14_000.0` and `520.0`.

7. **Add unit tests for smoke judging** in `crates/tools/src/perf.rs`:
   In `mod tests`, beside `every_measure_over_its_budget_fails_naming_its_median_p95_and_budget`:
   - `under_smoke_only_work_measures_over_budget_fail_naming_their_constants()`:
     Construct rows for all 7 `MEASURES` at `2.0 * measure.budget().0`. Call `judge_smoke(&rows)`.
     Assert that `failures.len() == 2`.
     Assert that messages for `VIEW_FOR_BYTES_BUDGET` and `FOLD_REDUCE_CALLS_BUDGET` are present with their median, p95, and constant name.
     Assert that none of the 5 timing budget constant names (`REDUCE_US_BUDGET_TEST`, `REDUCE_US_BUDGET_RELEASE`, `VIEW_FOR_US_BUDGET_TEST`, `VIEW_FOR_US_BUDGET_RELEASE`, `LEGAL_ACTIONS_US_BUDGET_TEST`, `LEGAL_ACTIONS_US_BUDGET_RELEASE`, `HASH_STATE_US_BUDGET_TEST`, `HASH_STATE_US_BUDGET_RELEASE`, `FOLD_MS_BUDGET_TEST`, `FOLD_MS_BUDGET_RELEASE`) appear in any message.
   - `under_smoke_measures_at_budget_pass()`:
     Construct rows for all 7 `MEASURES` at `measure.budget().0`. Call `judge_smoke(&rows)`.
     Assert `assert_eq!(judge_smoke(&rows), Vec::<String>::new());`.

8. **Update integration test and daily reason** in `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs`:
   - Module header (line 1-2): update to note that pull request smoke runs hold the two work budgets:
     `//! \`perf\` on the built \`jackioh\` (#3429): once per pull request holding the two work budgets, so the harness\n//! keeps working, and daily with every median held to the test profile's budgets.`
   - In `perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once`:
     Find `"view_for bytes"` and `"fold reduce calls"` rows in `rows`, and assert each median <= budget:
     ```rust
     let view_row = rows
         .iter()
         .find(|r| r["measure"] == "view_for bytes")
         .expect("view_for bytes row");
     assert!(
         view_row["median"].as_f64().unwrap() <= view_row["budget"].as_f64().unwrap(),
         "{view_row:#}"
     );
     let fold_row = rows
         .iter()
         .find(|r| r["measure"] == "fold reduce calls")
         .expect("fold reduce calls row");
     assert!(
         fold_row["median"].as_f64().unwrap() <= fold_row["budget"].as_f64().unwrap(),
         "{fold_row:#}"
     );
     ```
   - In `perf_holds_every_budget` (line 66), update the `#[ignore]` reason:
     `#[ignore = "daily: ten timed passes over the corpus held to the test profile's budgets; perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once holds the work budgets on every pull request"]`

9. **Update README documentation** in `crates/tools/README.md`:
   In the command table row for `perf [--smoke] [--json]`:
   Change `--smoke times one pass and judges nothing, as tests/perf.rs's per-pull-request test runs it; its daily test runs it judged`
   to `--smoke times one pass and judges the two work budgets, as tests/perf.rs's per-pull-request test runs it; its daily test runs it judged`.

10. **Verify with manual violation run**:
    Temporarily lower `FOLD_REDUCE_CALLS_BUDGET` below today's value (e.g. to `400.0`) or `VIEW_FOR_BYTES_BUDGET` (e.g. to `5000.0`).
    Run `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once` and verify it fails reporting the crossed budget.
    Restore the budget to its original value.

## Tests

- `crates/tools/src/perf.rs` (`mod tests`):
  - `nearest_rank_reads_the_median_and_the_p95`: existing test, unchanged, passes.
  - `spread_picks_evenly_spaced_actions`: existing test, unchanged, passes.
  - `every_measure_over_its_budget_fails_naming_its_median_p95_and_budget`: existing test, unchanged, passes.
  - `a_measure_at_its_budget_passes`: existing test, unchanged, passes.
  - `the_table_has_a_line_per_measure_under_its_header`: updated assertion for `; smoke: clock budgets not judged`, passes.
  - `under_smoke_only_work_measures_over_budget_fail_naming_their_constants`: new test asserting only work measures fail under smoke when all measures exceed budget.
  - `under_smoke_measures_at_budget_pass`: new test asserting empty failures under smoke when measures equal budget.
  Command: `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh perf::`
- `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs`:
  - `perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once`: asserts status success, report structure, and explicit median <= budget assertions for `"view_for bytes"` and `"fold reduce calls"`.
  Command: `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once`
- `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`:
  - `daily_every_ignored_test_says_it_runs_daily`: passes with updated `daily:` ignore message.
  - `readme_the_command_table_is_the_clis`: passes with updated README command table.
  Command: `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance -- daily readme`

## Done when

- [ ] Under `--smoke`, `view_for bytes` and `fold reduce calls` rows over budget fail with their constant names, and the command exits 1.
- [ ] Under `--smoke`, none of the five timing measures fails even when over budget.
- [ ] Full judged runs still evaluate and fail all seven measures over budget; existing unit tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] `perf_table` emits `; smoke: clock budgets not judged` under `--smoke`.
- [ ] Comments on `VIEW_FOR_BYTES_BUDGET` and `FOLD_REDUCE_CALLS_BUDGET` record the 2026-11-18 readings (7,001 bytes; 404 calls, fuzz seed 29).
- [ ] `crates/tools/README.md`, `crates/tools/src/perf.rs` module header, and `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs` headers are updated.
- [ ] `perf_holds_every_budget` `daily:` ignore reason names `perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once` holding work budgets per pull request.
- [ ] `perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once` passes on today's corpus and fails when a work budget is artificially lowered.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh perf::` passes.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf` passes.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance -- daily readme` passes.
- [ ] `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` passes.

## Risks

- **Breaking serde JSON serialization for `Row`:** Adding fields to `Row` could alter `jackioh perf --json`'s schema. Avoided by annotating `needs_clock` with `#[serde(skip)]`.
- **Accidental flakiness on shared CI runners:** Smoke tests run on single passes on shared GitHub Actions runners; judging timing budgets would cause flaky PR builds. Avoided by strictly filtering out clock-dependent measures under `--smoke`.
- **Breaking acceptance checks for README or daily ignores:** `acceptance.rs` scans `crates/tools/README.md` and `#[ignore = "daily: ..."]` strings. Avoided by keeping the command flags intact and adhering to the required `daily:` format.

## Open questions

None. The issue and proposal fully specify the behavior, naming, and budgets.

````markdown
## Goal

Under `--smoke`, `cargo jackioh perf` judges the two deterministic work measures (`VIEW_FOR_BYTES_BUDGET` and `FOLD_REDUCE_CALLS_BUDGET`) that require no clock and cannot flake, while leaving the five timing measures unjudged, exiting 1 if either work budget is crossed. The smoke table reports `; smoke: clock budgets not judged` in place of `; smoke: no budget judged`, and the work budgets' comments, docs, and test annotations record that smoke runs hold the work budgets on every pull request. Unit and integration tests verify both that crossing either work budget in smoke mode fails with the proper constant name and that timing budget violations remain ignored under smoke.

## Risks

- **Breaking serde JSON serialization for `Row`:** Adding fields to `Row` could alter `jackioh perf --json`'s schema. Avoided by annotating `needs_clock` with `#[serde(skip)]`.
- **Accidental flakiness on shared CI runners:** Smoke tests run on single passes on shared GitHub Actions runners; judging timing budgets would cause flaky PR builds. Avoided by strictly filtering out clock-dependent measures under `--smoke`.
- **Breaking acceptance checks for README or daily ignores:** `acceptance.rs` scans `crates/tools/README.md` and `#[ignore = "daily: ..."]` strings. Avoided by keeping the command flags intact and adhering to the required `daily:` format.
````
